claims.text: Role in MS: DMTs target the immune system to prevent exacerbations and delay disability;
claims.quote: Disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) target and control the immune system, to prevent exacerbations and delay eventual disability.

claims.text: highly efficacious: natalizumab, rituximab, ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, ublituximab, cladribine, alemtuzumab;
claims.quote: Highly efficacious: natalizumab, rituximab, ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, ublituximab, cladribine, and alemtuzumab.

claims.text: moderately efficacious: interferon beta 1a/1b, glatiramer, teriflunomide, fumarates, fingolimod and other S1P modulators;
claims.quote: Moderately efficacious: interferon beta 1a, interferon beta 1b, glatiramer acetate, teriflunomide, dimethyl fumurate, monomethyl fumurate, diroximel fumarate, fingolimod, siponimod, ozanimod, ponesimod

claims.text: growing consensus: high-efficacy tx first line at initiation; if one fails, try another.
claims.quote: There is growing consensus regarding using high-efficacy therapies as first line when initiating treatment.

claims.text: Natalizumab: monthly infusion; ↓exacerbations and new lesions but may ↑PML risk;
claims.quote: given as a monthly infusion, it reduces number of exacerbations and new brain lesions but may increase the risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML)

claims.text: PML Sx need an immediate brain MRI (w and w/o gadolinium).
claims.quote: Development of PML symptoms requires immediate brain MRI, with and without gadolinium.
